text:
incident-bot: PAGING: GeoDNS anomaly detected — sudden spike in NXDOMAINs from Cloudflare resolver clusters in eu-west-1. Affected backend: api.redwood-inference.com. Severity: P1. Auto-escalate to on-call. Logs: geo-dns-probe > 90% NXDOMAIN over last 3m.

alice: ack — i'm on it. pulling resolver traces & route53 change history.

ben: seen this too, customers in EU reporting 502/503 for model endpoints. adding ingress logs now.

carol: throwing up a quick query from an affected EU host: 
```
$ dig @1.1.1.1 api.redwood-inference.com +short || echo NXDOMAIN
NXDOMAIN
```
Looks like resolver cache giving NXDOMAIN intermittently.

alice: hypothesis: TTL race + Cloudflare edge returning SERVFAIL/NXDOMAIN while route53 updates were partially propagated during an autoscaling of geo weights. Checking route53 change-batch and our geodns policy.

ben: pulling Route53 change IDs now, one change about 7m ago (weight adjust for canary). change-id: Z123ABC.

prod-support: customer impact: ~1200 requests/min failing from EU, several enterprise customers reported errors to support. tagging severity as customer-impact > high.

mike: oncall handoff in 10m. alice, if you need me earlier ping @mike.

oncall-bot: @mike, you have been assigned the incident (rotation-sre). Please acknowledge.

mike: acknowledged. joining. quick ask: can we flip geodns fallback to prefer route53 primary for eu region temporarily?

alice: yes — plan: 1) set geodns fallback to prefer route53-origin (roll forward config) 2) increase query TTL to 60s? actually lower TTL to 30s to reduce cache divergence while we stabilize? thinking: lower TTL short-term so caches refresh from corrected records quickly. 3) enable additional resolver health-checks.

carol: lowering TTL might increase queries but helps slope. i'm for TTL=30s for 10m then evaluate.

ben: executing step 1 now — applying policy patch to geodns controller: 
```bash
# apply fallback weight to route53 for eu region
kubectl -n infra exec geodns-controller -- ./geodnsctl set-fallback --region eu-west-1 --prefer route53 --reason "incident 1777777777"
```
Applying... response: OK (propagating).

alice: verifying via dig once policy change propagates.

(2 minutes later)

carol: quick check: dig now returns A records consistently from route53 when using 1.1.1.1 and google resolvers in eu-west. initial NXDOMAIN spike trending down.

mike: rolling TTL change. executing: 
```bash
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id ZHOST123 --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.redwood-inference.com","Type":"A","TTL":30,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"3.12.45.6"}]}}]}'
```
Change submitted. Change status: PENDING.

ben: note — Cloudflare's resolvers sometimes cache NXDOMAIN based on negative TTL (SOA TTL). if upstream SOA negative TTL is high we might still see NXDOMAINs. checking SOA values.

alice: good catch. SOA negative TTL on our records was 300s from an older template. that's likely the race cause. changing SOA negative TTL to 30s as well.

carol: applying SOA patch. 
```bash
# update SOA negative TTL
kubectl -n infra exec dns-zone-manager -- update-soa --zone api.redwood-inference.com --min-ttl 30
```
Patch applied.

(5 minutes later)

prod-support: customer error rate dropped ~85% in EU over last 5m. some residual errors for customers behind stale resolvers.

mike: status update for execs: mitigation in place — geodns fallback forced to route53 for eu-west, TTLs lowered to 30s, SOA negative cached TTL reduced. monitoring for 15m.

alice: continuing to watch. capturing traces for a sample of failing flows to correlate with resolver IPs. earliest NXDOMAINs from Cloudflare LHR-1 cluster.

ben: i can see a cluster of stale answers from resolver 173.245.58.0/24 returning NXDOMAIN for queries that should resolve. trying to reach Cloudflare NOC contact.

carol: reached out to Cloudflare support via portal ticket INC-CF-9982 and included dig + tcpdump. they acknowledged and are investigating caching behavior on their EU edge.

oncall-bot: @mike handoff reminder in 5m.

mike: i'll stay on till handoff. next steps: keep fallback to route53 until cloudflare confirms cleanup and our negative TTL has fully propagated (should be under 10m). after stable period, revert TTL/soa to baseline via controlled change.

(10 minutes later)

prod-support: Fresh update from Cloudflare: they observed a partial cache poisoning/corruption on specific PoPs causing NXDOMAINs; they've purged caches and asked us to keep low negative TTL for 15m.

alice: good. maintain TTL 30s for 15m then raise to 60s then baseline 300s after 1h if stable. documenting rollback steps.

ben: i've recorded the change-ids and diffs, attaching logs to the incident ticket.

mike: customer notification draft: "We're aware of DNS resolution errors affecting EU customers. Mitigation applied (GeoDNS fallback and TTL adjustments). We're monitoring and will follow up with root cause and timeline." anyone want to add details?

carol: add that Cloudflare purged caches and we're collaborating on postmortem. mention impacted window and that some clients behind stale resolvers may still see errors briefly.

mike: sending notification now. 

(30 minutes later)

prod-support: metrics look stable, request error rate back to baseline for EU. no new alerts.

alice: preparing RCA notes: root cause = TTL/negative-TTL mismatch combined with in-flight route53 weight change + Cloudflare cache corruption in select PoPs leading to transient NXDOMAIN flood. Contributing: outdated SOA template with long negative TTL, and a concurrent geodns weight change.

ben: proposed remediation: 1) audit SOA negative TTLs across zones and standardize to <=60s for geo records; 2) change geodns weight rollouts to use ramped canary with health-check gating; 3) add resolver-probe to detect NXDOMAIN spikes per-POP and auto-fallback quicker.

mike: agreed. i'll open follow-up action items and assign owners. thanks all — handing off to next rotation in 10m.

oncall-bot: @mike has handed off incident to next oncall (rotation-sre).

mike: handoff complete. Incident moving to monitoring mode. will draft postmortem tomorrow.

carol: noted — prepping timeline & logs.

(incident archived after 2h)

prod-support: final note for ticket — impacted window 1777777777 -> 1777779050. customers with persistent issues should clear resolver cache or switch to different upstream for time being.

alice: thanks team.
